protocol.name: treeland_output_mirror_manager_unstable_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2024 - 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
This protocol lets a privileged client such as the DDE display settings panel organize physical outputs into mirroring groups: one source output whose rendered content is duplicated to one or more mirror outputs, so that several screens show the same desktop. This is the "copy mode" of the compositor, as opposed to the default "extension" mode where each output shows an independent desktop region.
The protocol exposes a singleton manager global that creates and tracks treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 objects. Each group designates a single source output and an ordered list of mirror outputs, all addressed by opaque uuid strings. Clients obtain the uuid of an output from the treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 protocol. An output may belong to at most one group at a time. A group drives copy mode while it has both a source and at least one mirror; a group with no source or no mirrors is inert and the affected outputs behave as normal extension outputs. An empty uuid represents the absence of a source; output uuids are never empty.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_output_mirror_manager_v1
interface.description:
A singleton global that creates treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 objects and broadcasts the set of existing groups to bound clients.
On bind the compositor emits one group_added event per existing group; when any client creates a group every other bound client receives group_added for it, and when a group is dissolved every bound client receives group_removed. Clients therefore never poll for the group set.
The protocol is intended for a single privileged client such as the DDE display settings panel. Multiple clients may bind concurrently for observation, but concurrent conflicting edits from several clients are not supported and may fail with fatal protocol errors.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the manager object.

entry.name: invalid_name
entry.summary: the group name is empty, not valid UTF-8, contains a NUL byte, or is rejected by the compositor

entry.name: name_exists
entry.summary: a group with the requested name already exists

entry.name: invalid_source
entry.summary: the non-empty source uuid does not identify a connected enabled output

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_output_mirror_manager_v1 object and release the client's binding to the manager global.
Existing treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 objects are not affected and remain valid until they are destroyed or the compositor dissolves the group. The client must destroy each group object separately; the compositor does not cascade destruction from the manager.

request.name: create_group

description.summary: create a new output mirror group

request.description:
Create a new treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 object with the given name and initial source output. An empty source creates a group with no source; the client adds mirrors afterwards with add_output and may change the source with set_source. Copy mode engages once the group has both a source and at least one mirror.
The name identifies the group in group_added and group_removed events. It must be a non-empty UTF-8 string without a NUL byte; an empty, non-UTF-8, or NUL-containing name, or one the compositor considers too long, is rejected with the invalid_name fatal error. A name that already identifies an existing group is rejected with the name_exists fatal error. A non-empty source that does not identify a connected enabled output is rejected with the invalid_source fatal error. These checks are deterministic, so the compositor raises them on the manager object and does not create the group.
On success the compositor broadcasts a group_added event carrying a new group object to every other bound client; the caller receives its group object only as the new_id return value and does not get a group_added event for it.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: unique UTF-8 name for the group

arg.name: source
arg.summary: uuid of the initial source output, or empty for no source

event.name: group_added
event.description:
Emitted when a mirror group is created by any client. Each bound client receives this event once per existing group on bind, and again whenever a new group is created — except for the client that created the group, which receives the group object as the new_id return value of create_group instead.
The id argument is a fresh group object; the compositor sends the initial source and output_added state of the group on it immediately after this event. The client may destroy the object if it does not need to observe that group; doing so does not dissolve the group.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: a group object bound to the new group

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the name of the new group

event.name: group_removed
event.description: Emitted when a mirror group is dissolved, whether because a client sent the dissolve request or because the compositor removed it as a whole. Every bound client receives this event for the group; any group objects that client holds for it receive a removed event and must be destroyed afterwards.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the name of the dissolved group

interface.name: treeland_output_mirror_group_v1
interface.description:
Represents one mirroring group: a source output, identified by its uuid, whose content is duplicated to an ordered list of mirror outputs, each identified by its uuid. Output uuids come from the treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 protocol and are never empty; an empty uuid in events represents the absence of a source.
The group keeps a source (zero or one) and an ordered mirror list (zero or more). An output may belong to at most one group; one already in another group fails with the output_in_use failure. The client builds the group with set_source and add_output in any order. Copy mode is engaged while the group has both a source and at least one mirror; otherwise the group is inert and the affected outputs behave as normal extension outputs.
Requests that cannot be applied because of transient output state (e.g. an output unplugged between get_uuid and the request) are reported via a non-fatal operation_failed event; the group is unchanged and the client may retry. Only already_dissolved — sending any request other than destroy on a dissolved group — is a fatal protocol error.
On creation the compositor sends the current state: one source event (empty uuid if no source) followed by one output_added event per mirror in list order. Later changes are reported by further source, output_added, and output_removed events.
Several group objects may be bound to the same group, for example one from create_group and others from group_added; they all observe the same state. Destroying one object only releases that client's handle. The dissolve request tears down the group as a whole, emitting removed to every bound group object and group_removed on the manager. After removed the object is inert: only destroy is valid, and anything else is rejected with the already_dissolved error.
When a member output is unplugged or disabled the compositor updates the group automatically: it emits output_removed for a removed mirror, and if the source is removed with mirrors remaining, the first remaining mirror becomes the new source (output_removed then source for it); if no mirrors remain, a source event with an empty uuid is emitted. Client-driven remove_output of the source, by contrast, clears it without auto-selecting a successor.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the group object.

entry.name: already_dissolved
entry.summary: the group has been dissolved; only destroy may be sent

enum.name: failure
enum.description: Returned by the operation_failed event when a set_source, add_output, or remove_output request cannot be applied. These reflect transient or dynamic output state (e.g. an output unplugged between get_uuid and the request), not a protocol violation; the client may retry or adjust and the connection is not terminated.

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: no enabled output with the provided uuid is currently connected

entry.name: duplicate_output
entry.summary: the output is already the source or a mirror of this group

entry.name: output_in_use
entry.summary: the output is the source or a mirror of another mirror group

entry.name: not_in_group
entry.summary: the output is not a member of this group

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy this group object and release the client's handle. The group itself is not affected: copy mode continues, other handles remain valid, and the compositor does not emit group_removed. Use dissolve to tear down the group as a whole. It is safe to destroy an object that has already received the removed event.

request.name: set_source
request.description:
Set the output identified by the given uuid as the source of the group, replacing any current source, which is removed and becomes a normal extension output again.
If the request cannot be applied, the compositor emits an operation_failed event and the group is unchanged: invalid_output if the uuid does not identify a connected enabled output, duplicate_output if the output is already in this group (to promote a current mirror to the source, remove it first with remove_output), or output_in_use if the output belongs to another group.
If the group already has mirrors, this engages or updates copy mode immediately. The compositor confirms the new source by emitting a source event.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the output to designate as the source

request.name: add_output
request.description:
Append the output identified by the given uuid to the end of the group's mirror list.
If the request cannot be applied, the compositor emits an operation_failed event and the group is unchanged: invalid_output if the uuid does not identify a connected enabled output, duplicate_output if the output is already in this group, or output_in_use if it belongs to another group.
If the group already has a source, this engages or extends copy mode immediately, confirmed by an output_added event. Sources and mirrors may be set in any order; copy mode engages once both are present.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the output to add as a mirror

request.name: remove_output
request.description:
Remove the output identified by the given uuid from the group. If the output is not a current member, the compositor emits an operation_failed event with not_in_group and the group is unchanged.
If the output is a mirror, an output_removed event is emitted for it; if the group then has a source but no mirrors, copy mode exits while the source remains set.
If the output is the source, the source is cleared and a source event with an empty uuid is emitted; the mirrors are unchanged and copy mode exits. This does not auto-select a successor; to promote a mirror, call set_source on it.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the member output to remove

request.name: dissolve

description.summary: dissolve the group and exit copy mode

request.description: Tear down the group: exit copy mode, remove it from the manager, and release the affected outputs. The compositor emits removed to every group object bound to this group and group_removed on the manager. After removed the object is inert; only destroy is valid, and anything else — including dissolve again — is rejected with already_dissolved.

event.name: source

description.summary: current source output of the group

event.description: Reports the uuid of the current source output. Emitted once on creation (empty uuid when the group has no source) and again whenever the source changes.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the current source output, or empty when the group has no source

event.name: output_added
event.description: Reports that an output was appended to the mirror list. Emitted once per existing mirror in list order on creation, and again whenever add_output succeeds.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the mirror output that was added

event.name: output_removed
event.description: Reports that an output left the mirror list. Emitted when a client removes a mirror, when a mirror is unplugged or disabled, or when a mirror is promoted to the source after the previous source was removed.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the mirror output that was removed

event.name: removed
event.description: Emitted to every group object bound to the group when the group is dissolved. After this event the object is inert and the client must destroy it.

event.name: operation_failed

description.summary: a set_source, add_output, or remove_output request failed

event.description: Emitted when a set_source, add_output, or remove_output request cannot be applied because of a transient or dynamic output state, such as an output being unplugged between get_uuid and the request. The code identifies the failure cause; the uuid is the output the client passed to the failing request. The group state is unchanged and the client may retry or adjust. This is not a protocol error and the connection is not terminated.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: the uuid the client passed to the failing request
